card.band: 4h. The operators share scheduler and subscription teardown semantics, with many per-operator edge cases such as config objects, completion and error ordering, and unsubscribe timing. Frontier agents get the basic operators, but the config-heavy ones (throttle, timeout, windowTime) are where they average lower. A weaker model gets only the simple operators.
card.cheat: Recalling upstream source from memory is possible but allowed. The hidden tests use new marble diagrams, not the public ones, and the snapshot has no git history or node_modules copy of rxjs.
card.grading: Hidden marble-test files for the removed operators (hundreds of cases through TestScheduler) plus the existing suite as a regression gate. The shipped base fails every graded case. Reward is the fraction passed.
card.reference: The removed upstream code, about 2-3k lines of TypeScript. It passes every hidden case.
card.task: /app ships a history-less snapshot of rxjs with the scheduler layer (asap, async, queue, animationFrame, VirtualTime) and the time operators (debounceTime, throttle, auditTime, bufferTime, windowTime, timeout, delay, sampleTime, timestamp and related) removed and stubbed. The agent rebuilds them against the public API.

spike_plan.kill_if: Recalled code passes at least 85% of fresh marble cases, confirming K8 (too easy because the operators are recalled)
spike_plan.pass_if: Recalled code fails at least 40% of fresh marble cases, showing that recall does not reach the reference
steps: In a networked throwaway container, clone ReactiveX/rxjs and check out 54796b38; confirm the scheduler and time-operator source files exist at that commit.
Run the existing vitest suite with a JSON or spec reporter and record per-test results, since the smoke probe produced no report.
Without network or repo access, prompt a model to write throttleTime and timeout from memory against the public API, then run 20 fresh marble diagrams through TestScheduler.
Measure the pass rate on those fresh diagrams; compare against the upstream code, which should pass all of them.
Check whether the rebuilt code passes all fresh cases on the first try, which would confirm recall shortcut.

v1.summary: Seed S-im-028 is a real, licensed (Apache-2.0) pinned rxjs commit whose removed scheduler and time operators are public, famous upstream code, so frontier agents could recall them near-verbatim and reach the reference, making it too easy (K8) and weakly sealed. Smoke probe was amber (build ok, all three test runs exited 1 with no report), so any rebuild would need custom per-test grading.
